parameters.tool: Select a tool from your library. The tool's diameter will be used for calculations.
parameters.toolDiameter: The physical diameter of the cutting tool. This is the most critical value for accurate offsets.
parameters.passes: Number of offset passes to create. More passes clear more copper but take longer.
parameters.stepOver: Percentage of the tool diameter to overlap on each pass. 50% is a good default.
parameters.combineOffsets: Merge all offset passes into a single geometry. Reduces G-code complexity but loses individual pass control.
parameters.millHoles: If checked, generates circular milling paths inside any drill holes larger than the tool. If unchecked, generates a simple peck/drill at the center.
parameters.cutSide: Where the tool sits relative to the polygon outline. Outside clears material around the shape. Inside clears within. On Path centers the tool on the line.
parameters.cutDepth: Final target depth for all cuts, relative to the material surface (Z=0). Should be a negative value (e.g., -0.05mm).
parameters.depthPerPass: Incremental depth of each pass when using multi-depth cutting. Smaller = gentler on tool.
parameters.multiDepth: Enable multiple passes at different depths for deep cuts. Reduces tool stress.
parameters.feedRate: Speed at which the tool moves while cutting (mm/min or in/min).
parameters.plungeRate: Speed at which the tool descends into material (mm/min or in/min). Usually slower than feed rate.
parameters.spindleSpeed: Rotation speed of the spindle (RPM). Higher speeds for smaller tools.
parameters.spindleDwell: Time in seconds to wait. Essential for high inertia spindles that need extra time to come up to speed.
parameters.direction: Climb milling: tool rotation matches feed direction (better finish). Conventional: opposite direction (more stable).
parameters.entryType: How the tool enters the material. Plunge: straight down. Ramp: diagonal. Helix: spiral down.
parameters.cannedCycle: Pre-programmed drill cycle. G83 (peck drilling) retracts periodically to clear chips.
parameters.peckDepth: Depth to drill before retracting when using peck drilling. Smaller = more retracts = cleaner holes.
parameters.dwellTime: Pause duration at bottom of hole (seconds). Allows chips to clear and reduces burrs.
parameters.retractHeight: Height to retract to between holes. Should clear board but minimize travel time.
parameters.tabs: Number of small tabs to leave uncut, holding the board in place.
parameters.tabWidth: The length of each holding tab in mm.
parameters.tabHeight: The thickness of the tab. A value of -0.5mm on a -1.8mm cut will leave a 0.5mm thick tab.
parameters.startCode: Custom Preamble to add to the beginning of this operation's command stream.
parameters.endCode: Custom Postamble to add to the end of this operation's command stream.
parameters.laserSpotSize: The effective diameter of the focused laser beam on the material surface. This is a reference - change it in Machine Settings.
parameters.laserIsolationWidth: Total width of copper to ablate around traces, measured from the trace edge outward. The number of laser passes is automatically calculated from this value, the spot size, and the step-over percentage.
parameters.laserSpacingMode: Choose how to define the distance between consecutive laser passes. Step Over uses a percentage of spot size. Lines/cm and LPI set the density directly.
parameters.laserLinesPerCm: Number of laser passes per centimetre. Higher values produce denser coverage.
parameters.laserLinesPerInch: Number of laser passes per inches. Higher values produce denser coverageance.
parameters.laserStepOver: Percentage of the spot diameter that adjacent paths overlap. Lower values (more overlap) give better copper removal but increase processing time. 50% is a good starting point; reduce to 30% if streaks appear.
parameters.laserClearStrategy:
How the laser fills areas that need copper removal.

• Filled Polygon: Exports solid shapes - your laser software handles the fill pattern. SVG only.
• Offset Paths: Concentric paths shrinking inward. Most reliable for streak prevention.
• Parallel Hatch: Straight lines at a fixed angle. Fast but single-direction.
• Hatch: Perpendicular sets of lines. More passes shift the angle between each other.
parameters.laserHatchAngle: Angle of the hatch lines in degrees. For parallel hatch, lines run at this angle. For cross-hatch, the second set runs perpendicular (angle + 90°). 45° is a good default - it crosses both horizontal and vertical traces.
parameters.laserCutSide:
Where the laser kerf falls relative to the board outline.

• Outside: Laser cuts outside the line (board stays full size).
• Inside: Laser cuts inside the line (board shrinks by kerf).
• On Line: Laser follows the exact line (board shrinks by half the kerf on each side).
parameters.stencilOffset: Shrinks (negative) or expands (positive) the stencil apertures. -0.05mm is a common default to prevent solder bridging.
parameters.stencilIgnoreRegions: If checked, ignores large copper pours and traces, only generating apertures for actual component pads (flashes).
parameters.stencilExcludeDrillPads: Automatically removes stencil apertures that sit directly over through-holes to prevent solder paste from falling into the holes.
parameters.stencilAddRegHoles: Generates 4 circular alignment holes outside the board boundaries to help pin the stencil in place during manual application.
parameters.stencilRegDiameter: The physical diameter of the registration pins/dowels you plan to use.
parameters.stencilRegMargin: How far outside the calculated board boundary to place the registration holes.
parameters.detectNesting: When enabled, shapes fully contained inside other shapes are treated as holes and subtracted from the outer boundary during offset generation.
parameters.pocketStrategy: How the pocket interior is cleared. Concentric Offsets shrinks inward in passes. Raster sweeps back and forth in straight lines.
parameters.rasterAngle: Angle of the sweep lines for raster pocketing. 0° is horizontal, 90° vertical, 45° diagonal.
parameters.rasterBidirectional: When checked the tool cuts in both directions. When unchecked it lifts and returns after each line for climb-only cutting.
parameters.continuousSpiral: Connects concentric offset passes into one continuous spiral, eliminating retract moves between rings.
parameters.drillStepOver: Percentage of the tool diameter to overlap on each concentric milling ring inside oversize holes.
parameters.vbitAngle: The included angle of the V-bit. Common values are 60, 90, and 120 degrees. Determines cut width at a given depth.
parameters.vcarveFlatDepth: Depth for flat areas wider than the V-bit can reach. Set to 0 to skip flat clearing.
parameters.useVcarveClearingTool: Use a separate flat end mill to rough out wide flat areas before the V-bit finishes the edges.
parameters.finishingPass: Adds a final light pass at full depth with reduced stepover for a smoother pocket floor.
parameters.finishStepover: Stepover percentage for the finishing pass. Lower values give a better surface finish.
parameters.spotDrill: Plunge a shallow pilot hole at each location before the main drilling pass. Improves accuracy on curved or uneven surfaces.
parameters.spotDepth: Depth of the spot drill pilot hole.
parameters.vcarveMaxDepth: Maximum allowed depth for V-carve cuts. Limits how deep the V-bit plunges into wide features.
parameters.vcarveStartDepth: Starting depth offset. Use to engrave below an existing pocket floor.
parameters.rotaryKinematics: Radial turns the part continuously under the tool for smooth round surfaces. Indexed 3+1 rotates to a fixed angle, mills that face flat, then rotates again. Indexed needs a post with an A or B word; radial can also run on a machine with the rotary wired to the Y driver.
parameters.rotaryAxis: Which machine axis the part rotates about. X gives an A word, Y gives a B word. Must match how the rotary is physically mounted and what your post-processor declares.
parameters.rotaryModelUp: How the model sits in the scene before it is laid onto the rotary. Choose Upright if the model was designed standing in Z; it will be laid down onto the axis for you. Choose Along if it is already lying along the rotary axis.
parameters.rotaryStockShape: Cross-section of the raw blank. Round starts cutting at the blank diameter. Square starts at the corner radius and turns the stock round on the way down, which adds roughing time but saves you pre-turning it.
parameters.rotaryBlankDiameter: Outside diameter of the raw stock. Leave at 0 to fit the blank to the model automatically. Setting it smaller than the model flattens everything outside it, so only reduce it if the stock really is smaller.
parameters.rotaryAxisOffsetB: Shifts the rotation axis sideways from the model's own centre, in the first cross direction. Use it when the model was not modelled centred on its axis. Leave at 0 for a centred model.
parameters.rotaryAxisOffsetC: Shifts the rotation axis in the second cross direction (workspace Z). Same purpose as the first offset. Leave at 0 for a centred model.
parameters.rotaryHoldingMode: Between Centers assumes a tailstock supports the far end, so material past that end is protected. Chuck Only assumes the part is cantilevered and the far end is open air.
parameters.rotaryChuckEndMode: What happens where the model ends at the chuck. Stop at geometry is the default and the reliable choice: the waste is turned down to the minimum radius and the tool stops at the part. Roll Over leaves a small lip around the edge, but only works on an end that is flat and close to square against the axis - a slanted, domed or off-centre end will show a scalloped ring, and you will get a warning. Taper cones down to the drive stub instead of stepping.
parameters.rotaryChuckEndMm: Moves where the chuck end of the model is treated as ending, along the axis. Negative stops short of the real edge - use it for a slanted base or a tangent slope your tool cannot enter cleanly. Positive machines further past it, turning the waste down to the minimum radius as it goes. Too large a negative value leaves nothing to machine and you will get a warning. On Roll Over and Taper this is the lip depth or cone length instead, and is always positive.
parameters.rotaryTailEndMode: What happens where the model ends at the tailstock. Stop at geometry is the default and the reliable choice: the waste is turned down to the minimum radius and the tool stops at the part. Roll Over leaves a small lip around the edge, but only works on an end that is flat and close to square against the axis - a slanted, domed or off-centre end will show a scalloped ring, and you will get a warning. Taper cones down to the drive stub instead of stepping.
parameters.rotaryTailEndMm: Moves where the tailstock end of the model is treated as ending, along the axis. Negative stops short of the real edge - use it for a slanted top or a tangent slope your tool cannot enter cleanly. Positive machines further past it, turning the waste down to the minimum radius as it goes. Too large a negative value leaves nothing to machine and you will get a warning. On Roll Over and Taper this is the lip depth or cone length instead, and is always positive.
parameters.rotaryMinRadius: Radius of the drive stub the tool never cuts into: what a chuck grips and a tailstock centre bears on. It is also the radius a Taper end cones down to. On Indexed 3+1 it applies as a cylinder about the centreline, so a value here is a hard floor on how deep any face can go near the axis - the default 2mm keeps a 2mm core no face will cut through. Set it to 0 for a free end you want to part right through.
parameters.rotaryDepth: How deep to cut below the blank surface, measured as radius. Leave at 0 to follow the model down to its own thinnest point. Auto depth near the rotation axis makes generation very slow, so set an explicit value on tall models.
parameters.rotaryToolShape: Shape of the cutting tip. Ball nose gives the smoothest curved surfaces. Flat leaves scallops on curves but cuts flats cleanly. Bull nose is a flat endmill with a rounded corner.
parameters.rotaryCornerRadius: Corner radius of a bull nose tool. Only used when the tip shape is Bull Nose. Must be less than half the tool diameter.
parameters.rotaryMode: Which passes to generate. Roughing removes bulk in constant-radius layers. Finishing follows the surface. Both runs them in order with a single tool.
parameters.rotaryRoughAxis: Direction the roughing scanlines run. Along the axis suits long slender parts. Around the circumference suits short stubby ones and keeps the tool engaged more evenly.
parameters.rotaryRoughStepdown: How much radius each roughing layer removes. Smaller is gentler on the tool and takes longer. Around a third of the tool diameter is a safe starting point.
parameters.rotaryRoughStepoverPct: Distance between roughing scanlines, as a percentage of tool diameter. 45% is a good default for roughing.
parameters.rotaryRoughStock: Material left on the surface by roughing for the finishing pass to remove. 0.3mm is a good default. Too little and roughing marks show through, too much and finishing works hard.
parameters.rotaryFinishPattern: Spiral is one continuous helix with a single entry and no witness lines, and is the best default. Along the axis suits parts with axial features. Around cuts closed rings and suits parts with rotational detail.
parameters.rotaryFinishStepoverPct: Distance between finishing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter. 10% gives a fine finish. Larger values are faster but leave visible scallops.
parameters.rotaryCellSize: Size of one sampling cell on the model surface. Leave at 0 to derive it from the resolution setting below. Setting it manually overrides that and can make generation very slow on large parts.
parameters.rotaryGridMaxDim: Sampling resolution along the longest dimension of the model, used when cell size is automatic. Higher captures finer detail and takes longer. 1024 suits most work.
parameters.indexedFaceCount: How many flat faces to mill around the part. More faces approximate a round surface more closely but multiply machining time. Four suits a square blank, six or eight a pre-turned round one.
parameters.indexedStartAngle: Rotates the whole set of faces. Use it to line the first face up with a feature on the model, or to put the parting line somewhere you do not mind seeing it.
parameters.indexedBlankWidth: Distance across the flats of the raw blank. Leave at 0 to derive it from the model. Anything on the model that sticks out past the blank cannot be reached and is flattened, so raise this if the part is larger than you declared.
parameters.indexedDepth: How deep each face may cut below the blank face plane. Leave at 0 to reach just past the rotation axis, which is as deep as one face can usefully go - anything further belongs to the opposing face. Set a value only to stop shallower than that.
parameters.indexedAxisOvercut: How far past the rotation axis each face may cut. Opposing faces that stop exactly on the axis are tangent, not overlapping, so backlash or a touch-off error leaves a spine on the centreline. Leave at 0 for one tool radius automatically. This deepens the waste only - it never cuts into the minimum-radius drive stub, so you can set both.
parameters.indexedRoughStepdown: How much depth each roughing layer removes on a face. Smaller is gentler on the tool and takes longer. Around a third of the tool diameter is a safe starting point.
parameters.indexedRasterAxis: Direction the finishing lines run on each face. Along the rotary axis gives long uninterrupted passes. Across the face suits parts whose detail runs around the part rather than along it.
parameters.indexedCrossFinish: Adds a second finishing pass at 90 degrees to the first. Roughly doubles finishing time and noticeably improves the surface on curved faces.
parameters.indexedCollisionGuard: Limits tip depth so the shank and holder cannot touch the surface. Needs cuttingLength, shankDiameter, holderDiameter and holderStickout on the tool record; skipped silently without them.
parameters.vbitTipDiameter: Flat width at the very tip of the bit. 0 is a perfect point; a real bit usually has a small flat.
parameters.vcarveClearingTool: Flat end mill used to rough out the wide flats before the V-bit finishes the edges.
parameters.vcarveSimplifyTolerance: Maximum deviation allowed when straightening the medial-axis path.
parameters.vcarveMinChainLength: Drops carve chains shorter than this. Removes specks left by noisy outlines.
parameters.vcarveCornerAngle: Turn angle above which a vertex counts as a corner and gets its own plunge.
parameters.reliefToolShape: Tip geometry the compensator models. Ball follows curves best, flat is faster on shallow relief, bull nose is a flat with a corner radius.
parameters.reliefCornerRadius: Corner radius of a bull-nose cutter. Ignored for ball and flat tips.
parameters.reliefDepthMapping: Scaled stretches the model's height range to fit the carve depth - use it for artwork. Literal keeps the model's real millimetres - use it for dimensioned parts.
parameters.reliefDepth: Total carve depth below the surface. 0 uses the model's own height.
parameters.reliefStartDepth: Depth of the surface the relief starts from. Use it to carve inside an existing pocket floor.
parameters.reliefInvert: Cuts the negative of the model, so the result is a mould of it.
parameters.reliefBoundaryMode: What happens at the model's silhouette. Stop leaves the surrounding stock. Roll Over forms a wall down past the edge. Extend keeps cutting a set distance beyond it.
parameters.reliefBoundaryMm: How far past the silhouette the boundary is formed. Used by Roll Over and Extend.
parameters.reliefMaskUncovered: Only cuts where the model actually sits. Leave it off to clear the whole grid down to the floor.
parameters.reliefMode: Roughing removes bulk in flat layers, finishing rasters the surface. Both runs one after the other with the same tool.
parameters.reliefRoughStepdown: Z depth removed per roughing layer.
parameters.reliefRoughStepoverPct: Sideways step between roughing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter.
parameters.reliefRoughStock: Material left on the surface for the finishing pass to take off.
parameters.reliefFinishStepoverPct: Sideways step between finishing passes, as a percentage of tool diameter. Lower is smoother and slower.
parameters.reliefRasterAxis: Direction the passes sweep. Run them across the model's long details rather than along them.
parameters.reliefCrossFinish: Adds a second finishing pass at 90 degrees to the first. Roughly doubles finishing time and noticeably improves curved surfaces.
parameters.reliefSkipFloor: Skips the flat floor pass. Safe when roughing already clears the floor with the same tool.
parameters.reliefCellSize: Sampling grid pitch in mm. 0 derives it from the model size and the resolution cap below.
parameters.reliefGridMaxDim: Cap on the derived grid's longest side. Higher captures finer detail and costs slicing time and memory.
parameters.reliefSimplifyTolerance: Maximum deviation allowed when straightening finishing paths. Larger values give smaller G-code.
parameters.reliefMinSegmentLength: Drops roughing segments shorter than this. Removes stutter without changing the cut.

originControls.originOffset: Set a new X/Y origin. Click 'Apply Origin' to save this position as the new (0,0).
originControls.boardRotation: Apply a rotation (in degrees) to all files around itself.
originControls.mirrorGeometry: Invert file geometry. Usefull with bottom-layer isolation.

machineSettings.pcbThickness: The total thickness of your PCB material (e.g., 1.6mm). Used for cutout depth calculations.
machineSettings.safeZ: Maximum safe height for rapid moves and tool changes (G0). Must clear all clamps and fixtures.
machineSettings.travelZ: Height above the board (Z=0) where the tool travels between cutting paths.
machineSettings.rapidFeed: The feed rate (mm/min) for G0 rapid movements (travel and safe Z moves).
machineSettings.postProcessor: Selects the G-code dialect for your specific CNC controller (Non-Grbl modules need more testing, use with caution).
machineSettings.gcodeUnits: Sets the units for the exported G-code file (G21 for mm, G20 for inches).
machineSettings.rolandMachineModel: Select your Roland machine to auto-populate common settings (steps/mm, feed limits, Z mode). All fields remain editable after selection.
machineSettings.rolandStepsPerMM: Motor steps per millimeter of travel. Determines coordinate resolution. MDX-50/40A: 100, MDX-15/20: 40. Incorrect values scale all coordinates proportionally.
machineSettings.rolandZMode: 3D mode uses the Z command for simultaneous XYZ interpolation (MDX-40A and above). 2.5D mode uses PU/PD which only supports XY cutting at a fixed depth set by !PZ.
machineSettings.rolandMaxFeed: Maximum XY feed rate in mm/sec. The VS (velocity) command is clamped to this value. Exceeding it may cause the machine to reject or ignore commands.
machineSettings.rolandSpindleMode: 'Direct RPM' sends explicit speed values via !RC. 'Indexed' sends a preset 1-15 via !RC. 'Manual Only' means the machine has a fixed speed - software only controls on/off via !MC.
machineSettings.laserProfile: Select the target software you will use to cut the exported file. This automatically configures SVG grouping, layer colors, and DOM ordering to match what that specific software expects.
machineSettings.laserProfileColors: Click any swatch to override the default layer color for the current profile. These colors map to the power/speed settings in your target laser software.
machineSettings.laserSpotSize: The effective cut width of your laser beam. Manufacturer should list it in the speceification sheet. Typical values: UV laser 0.02-0.08mm, Fiber laser 0.03-0.15mm.
machineSettings.laserSvgGrouping: Determines how SVG paths are organized. 'By Layer' groups by operation, 'By Color' groups by assigned color, and 'None' outputs flat geometry.
machineSettings.laserReverseCutOrder: Orders the output from bottom to top. Required by LightBurn and xTool to process the first operation first.
machineSettings.laserHeatManagement: Sorts paths within a pass from smallest to largest area, allowing smaller details time to cool down before larger surrounding cuts.
machineSettings.laserColorPerPass: Automatically assigns a different color to each cutting pass. Useful for software that maps power/speed settings to colors.
machineSettings.laserExportFormat: SVG exports vector paths that laser software (LightBurn, RDWorks) interprets with its own power/speed settings per color layer. PNG exports a raster image at the specified DPI - useful for direct image engraving modes.
machineSettings.laserExportDPI: Resolution of the exported PNG image. Higher DPI gives finer detail but larger file size. 1000 DPI is suitable for most PCB work. Match this to your laser software's engraving resolution setting.
machineSettings.stencilExportPadding: Physical margin (in mm) added around the stencil geometry in the exported SVG. Provides breathing room for alignment on vinyl cutters and laser plotters.

vizPanel.grid: Toggle the visibility of the canvas grid.
vizPanel.wireframe: Render all geometry as thin outlines instead of filled shapes.
vizPanel.boardBounds: Show a box representing the total size of all loaded files.
vizPanel.rulers: Show/hide the rulers around the canvas.
vizPanel.offsets: Show/hide the calculated offset geometry. This is automatically hidden when a Preview is generated.
vizPanel.previews: Show/hide the toolpath previews, which represent the actual path of the tool.
vizPanel.fusionMode: Merge all overlapping isolation/clearing geometry. Required for Arc Reconstruction.
vizPanel.preprocessed: Shows the geometry *after* fusion but *before* arc reconstruction. Requires Fusion Mode.
vizPanel.preprocessedOffsets: Shows the raw offset polygon geometry before boolean operations and winding selection.
vizPanel.arcReconstruction: Attempt to rebuild arcs from line segments in fused geometry. Requires Fusion Mode.
vizPanel.debugPoints: Show all individual points in all geometry.
vizPanel.bwMode: Render the canvas in black and white, ignoring layer colors.
vizPanel.verboseDebug: Show extended 'debug' messages in the status log and browser console. Requires a page reload to see startup messages.

exporter.order: Drag and drop operations to set the final cutting order.
exporter.singleFile: Combine all selected operations into one G-code file. If unchecked, you will get one file per operation.
exporter.splitDrills: When enabled, peck drill operations are separated into individual files grouped by original hole diameter. Milled holes are exported together in their own file. Requires multi-file export mode.
exporter.includeComments: Add human-readable comments (e.g., '; Starting Operation: isolation.gbr') to the G-code.
exporter.toolChanges: Insert a pause (M0 or M6) when the tool changes between operations. (Not yet implemented)
exporter.optimize: Applies multiple algorithms to reduce operation time. Disable to try and remove unexpected toolpaths.
exporter.filename: The name of the G-code file that will be downloaded.
exporter.calculate: Process the selected operations and generate the G-code preview based on the current order and settings.
